answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond that is slashed when its messages are proven to violate protocol rules, with disputes resolved by a randomly selected jury of bonded agents. A single operator can still create many identities, but must lock capital in every one and risks losing it, so flooding the system raises the attacker’s cost rather than granting free influence. The bond can fund honest participants in a dune, oasis, or meadow market without treating names or device fingerprints as proof of uniqueness.
